nodes.title: Backward-selection chain at a nonempty set

nodes.summary: Unfolding `chain` at the empty set (the chain stops).
nodes.title: Backward-selection chain at the empty set

nodes.summary: Backward selection: the list of remaining sets `R₀ = R, R₁, …, ∅`, where `R_{t+1}` is `R_t` with the feature chosen by `pick` masked.
nodes.title: Backward-selection chain of remaining feature sets

nodes.summary: Proposition 1 (second part) of Carter et al.: among the sets met during backward selection, the returned SIS has the smallest cardinality among the sufficient ones.
nodes.title: Proposition 1 (second part)

nodes.summary: Proposition 1 (first part) of Carter et al.: no feature of the returned SIS can be additionally masked while keeping the prediction at or above the threshold.
nodes.title: Proposition 1 (first part)

nodes.summary: If the prediction on the starting set reaches the threshold, `findSIS` returns a set.
nodes.title: FindSIS returns a set when the start reaches the threshold

nodes.summary: For a monotone set function (masking more features never raises the prediction), the returned SIS is inclusion-minimal: no proper subset is sufficient. (Derived; the paper states only Proposition 1.)
nodes.title: Minimality of FindSIS for monotone set functions

nodes.summary: Criterion (1): the returned SIS is a subset of the starting features and is sufficient.
nodes.title: FindSIS returns a sufficient subset of the features

nodes.summary: `FindSIS`: un-mask features in reverse order of masking (start from `∅`) and return the first set on which the prediction reaches the threshold, or `none`. The paper's procedure does not test `∅` itself; the two agree whenever `g ∅ < τ`, the case the paper considers.
nodes.title: FindSIS procedure for sufficient input subsets

nodes.summary: `pick` is a greedy backward-selection rule for `g`: from a nonempty remaining set `R` it masks a feature `i ∈ R` maximizing `g (R.erase i)`.
nodes.title: Greedy backward-selection rule

nodes.summary: The starting set is the first set of the chain.
nodes.title: Starting set begins the backward-selection chain

nodes.summary: The sets of the SIS-collection are pairwise disjoint.
nodes.title: Sets of the SIS-collection are pairwise disjoint

nodes.summary: Proposition 2 of Carter et al.: if the fully masked input is below the threshold, masking every set of the SIS-collection leaves the prediction below the threshold.
nodes.title: Proposition 2

nodes.summary: Every set of the SIS-collection is a nonempty sufficient subset of the starting features.
nodes.title: Sets of the SIS-collection are nonempty and sufficient

nodes.summary: `SIScollection`: while the remaining features `R` are sufficient (`τ ≤ g R`), find a SIS among them, record it and mask it. Stops if `findSIS` returns an empty set (only possible when `τ ≤ g ∅`).
nodes.title: SIS-collection procedure

nodes.summary: Every set in the backward-selection chain is a subset of the starting set.
nodes.title: Sets in the backward-selection chain are subsets of the start

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
